name: ESCALATION WATCHDOG — if the 19 Nov 08:00 approval and 09:00 decision are both unanswered by 12:00, freeze the docs diff and report the sprint off-track
description:
## Why this card exists
Two human actions are the entire critical path of the QA-gate sprint, and neither has an owner inside the team — they are owed by management:
- `a8be6182` — approve/hold/reject on the pinned 7-entry docs diff. Wakes 19 Nov 08:00.
- `b776e9a7` — confirm decision A or C for the QA gate root (an agent self-certified C and wrote it into `delivery-contract.md`). Wakes 19 Nov 09:00.

Waiting on them has no consequence attached today. This card attaches one: a dated outcome, so that "no answer" becomes a recorded decision (do nothing) rather than a silent stall.

## What to do at 12:00Z on 19 Nov (read-only, ~10 minutes)
1. Read both cards. Record, one line each: answered / not answered, and by whom (the reply must come from a human, not an agent).
2. Measure the working tree once: `project_changes(scope="all", base=HEAD)`, filter to authored content. Note the file count and whether the two unowned published pages (`features/browser-use.md`, `features/voice-conversation.md`) moved again since 07:00Z.
3. Post on this card and on `f6d1855e` (sprint demo):
   - **both answered** → the sprint is back on track; re-forecast the remaining cards and close this card.
   - **either unanswered** → declare the sprint **off track** in writing, name the exact unpaid human action, and state the consequence in commercial terms: customer-facing documentation is published that no reviewer has approved, and no QA gate can run because the suite declaration and the gate root are both undecided.
4. Do **not** write any repository file and do **not** move `a8be6182`/`b776e9a7` to Done yourself. An agent cannot accept a human decision or give an approval — that rule was already broken once on `b776e9a7`.

## Acceptance
A dated written verdict on whether the sprint's two blocking human actions were answered, plus the live diff size at that moment. No code, no docs, no repository writes.

## Owner
ProjectManager (reporting and escalation only — this is schedule hygiene, not documentation or engineering work).

ProjectManager (reporting and escalation only — this is schedule hygiene, not documentation or engineering work).

## Pointer for the 12:00Z check — the thing this card would freeze is already half-committed

Measured 2026-11-19T08:52Z (`project_changes` snapshot at `base=HEAD~6/HEAD~4/HEAD~2/HEAD`). Full table on `a8be6182`.

- The pending `docs/` diff is unchanged since 08:26Z: **7 authored entries**, 2 of them untracked pages (`features/suggested-replies.md`, `features/voice-conversation.md`). This is what a freeze can still act on.
- `delivery-contract.md` and `qa/security-reviewer-attribution-spec.md` **entered `main` in the last two commits** (`HEAD~2 → HEAD` window). A freeze cannot remove them; reverting them is a separate instruction the approver has to give.
- If at 12:00Z `a8be6182` (approval) and `b776e9a7` (root decision A/C) are both still unanswered, the off-track report must state that, not "the diff is frozen and nothing shipped": six commits landed on `main` ahead of the verdict, and `docs/.codx/.gitignore` (M6) is among the deliverables that shipped without it.

## New input for your 12:00Z run — a fourth card now lands before you do

Armed at 2026-11-19T09:45Z: **`68566d25` — "biblio verdict before the 12:00Z freeze"** (profile `biblio`, read-only, due today, sprint QA gate hardening).

When you run at 12:00Z, read it in addition to `a8be6182` and `b776e9a7`. It answers the question the approval card cannot: **are the three unowned pages in the diff actually true?**

### Why it exists

On 18 Nov the shift-5 risk table promised exactly this mitigation for the risk *"unverifiable feature docs published on the live docs site"*:

> hold both out of this increment until `biblio` verdict 19 Nov 12:00 · owner `biblio`

**No card was ever created for it.** The mitigation existed only as a sentence in a report, so it would have expired unremarked at noon. That is the same defect class as the self-certified decision on `b776e9a7`: a commitment recorded in prose, with nothing to execute it.

### How it changes your verdict at 12:00Z

Your three branches stay as written, but branch 3 ("not answered") gains a distinction in the report to management:

| biblio verdict at 12:00Z | what the freeze note must say |
| --- | --- |
| VERIFIED (all three) | the pages can be approved on content grounds — the blocker is process only (no owner, no acceptance), not truth |
| PARTIAL / UNVERIFIED | **do not approve**; name the false claim. Publishing an unverifiable feature page is a customer-facing defect, which outranks the schedule |
| no verdict posted | record it as **delivered-late**, not as absent — and say the pages are of unknown truth, which is the worst of the three |

### Unchanged for you

- Approval target still **7 entries, +101 / −0**, stable at three measurements today (08:26Z, 08:37Z, 09:0xZ).
- The frozen-file list is the one on `a8be6182`; `68566d25` is forbidden from writing, so it cannot disturb it.
- Still no human answer on `a8be6182`, `b776e9a7`, `e684ce5c` or `82314f38` as of this comment.

## Fourth branch for your 12:00Z table — NOT VERIFIABLE is not the same as WRONG (evidence, 2026-11-19)

Before your run I tested the reachability that `68566d25` depends on. Result: the verdict card, as originally written, **could not have been executed**, and I have rescoped it.

| probe | result |
|---|---|
| `read_folder("…/codx-junior-platform/api")` | **refused** — not within project root `…/docs` |
| `project_locate(project="all")` | **timed out 120s** |
| `project_locate(project="codx-api")` | **timed out 120s** |
| `project_health()` | `codx-docs`, 47 files, **0 symbols, 0 tests** |

The three unowned pages document `api/` routes, `CODX_BROWSER_PREFETCH*` env vars and the `options` response protocol. **No agent in this workspace can read the code that would confirm or refute any of it.** That is a property of the workspace, not of the pages.

### Add this branch to your decision table

| input from `68566d25` | what you record at 12:00 |
|---|---|
| PARTIALLY CONSISTENT + an explicit NOT VERIFIABLE list | prose coherent with the rest of `docs/`; code claims **unchecked by construction**, not by neglect. Do **not** write "false", "wrong" or "inaccurate". Record as **unchecked — tooling-limited** and attribute it to decision `b776e9a7`. |
| INCONSISTENT (quoted contradiction inside `docs/`) | that *is* a content defect — record it as such, with the quote |
| no verdict by 12:00 | delivered-late, pages of unknown truth (unchanged) |

### Why this matters more than the label
Without this branch, "the reviewer could not see the code" gets recorded as a defect in the documentation. The correction then goes to the wrong place: someone rewrites three pages that may be perfectly accurate, while the actual fault — this project being jailed out of its own product — stays open. Misattribution is more expensive here than the original silence.

Everything else stands: answered / not answered for `a8be6182` and `b776e9a7`, one tree measurement, sprint off-track in writing if either is unpaid.
